name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft clumped earth with raised clods, gentle lighter dry and darker damp areas and small grit clusters running across tile borders
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-a

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain texture filling the full 96x80 area with no silhouette, no edge line, no eave shadow and no standing object. The column scans show only irregular alternation of earth tones (L about 60-118) with no band, ellipse or front face. It is a flat top-down ground field with no south face, which is expected for a terrain tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a seamless brown earth field with about 5 visible tones per tile (7 colours in total), which is above the grass reference (3 visible tones) and a little below the paving (7). Near-flat coverage is only 2%, so there are no large flat fills, and the clods, damp patches and grit are scattered across the field. There is no outline, and the dark edge pixels are tinted brown (0% neutral), so no sticker look. The weaknesses are that the whole patch uses only 7 colours in one narrow brown ramp, and the texture looks like repeated mottling with soft noise. It lacks the per-clump highlights and grain variety of the Beodeul grass, which has 80 colours and distinct tufts. Overall it is competent but a bit more uniform and thinner than a careful artist would accept next to the reference.

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless terrain texture of mottled brown earth with clods and grit that fills every row at full width (96 px for rows 0-79). It has no silhouette, no edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no front face. The column scans show only irregular light and dark noise runs of 1-18 rows, with no structural bands. This is a flat ground tile field, not a standing object, so the 3/4-view top-and-front rules do not apply. The kind (terrain) matches.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a seamless earth field with clods, lighter dry and darker damp areas, and grit. It has 5 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it is within the reference range. Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no real flat fills. There is no outline, which suits a ground tile, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so they carry a brown tint. The weakness is the small palette: only 7 colours in total, and the mottling reads as soft, repeated blotches. It lacks the per-clump highlights, the crisp pebble-by-pebble shading and the grain variety of the references. It is somewhat softer and less structured than the grass reference's distinct tufts and clusters, and it shows less variety than the paving's shaded stones. Clods are suggested more than modelled with a highlight edge and shadow side. A careful artist would likely accept it as a clean ground fill but would call it slightly thinner than the Beodeul standard. When in doubt, fail.
